Each test's expected output is the popcount of `XOR(nums) ^ k`, since the answer is the number of bits that must flip to turn the current XOR into `k`.

```json
[
  {"input": "[5]\n5", "output": "0"},
  {"input": "[5]\n2", "output": "3"},
  {"input": "[0]\n1", "output": "1"},
  {"input": "[1, 1, 1]\n0", "output": "1"},
  {"input": "[7, 8]\n0", "output": "4"},
  {"input": "[1000000]\n0", "output": "7"},
  {"input": "[10, 10, 10]\n10", "output": "0"},
  {"input": "[3, 5, 6]\n0", "output": "0"},
  {"input": "[1, 2, 4, 8]\n0", "output": "4"},
  {"input": "[12, 0, 0]\n3", "output": "4"}
]
```

The answer is the number of set bits in `(XOR of all nums) ^ k`. Each bit flip toggles exactly one bit of the overall XOR, so the minimum is the popcount of that difference. I worked each expected output from this rule by hand.

```json
[
  {"input": "[5]\n5", "output": "0"},
  {"input": "[1]\n0", "output": "1"},
  {"input": "[0]\n7", "output": "3"},
  {"input": "[1, 2, 4, 8]\n0", "output": "4"},
  {"input": "[3, 3]\n10", "output": "2"},
  {"input": "[1000000]\n0", "output": "7"},
  {"input": "[10, 20, 30]\n50", "output": "3"},
  {"input": "[7, 7, 7]\n7", "output": "0"},
  {"input": "[1, 1, 1, 1, 1]\n0", "output": "1"},
  {"input": "[6, 9]\n12", "output": "2"}
]
```

The minimum number of operations is the number of bits where the current XOR of `nums` differs from `k`. Each flip changes the total XOR by exactly one bit, so the answer is `popcount((XOR of nums) ^ k)`. I worked each expected output by hand from that rule.

```json
[
  {"input": "[1]\n0", "output": "1"},
  {"input": "[5]\n5", "output": "0"},
  {"input": "[0]\n7", "output": "3"},
  {"input": "[1, 2, 4, 8]\n0", "output": "4"},
  {"input": "[10, 6]\n3", "output": "4"},
  {"input": "[1000000]\n0", "output": "7"},
  {"input": "[0, 0, 0]\n1000000", "output": "7"},
  {"input": "[3, 3, 3]\n3", "output": "0"},
  {"input": "[7, 8]\n1", "output": "3"},
  {"input": "[1, 2, 3]\n5", "output": "2"}
]
```
